title: CTEs and subqueries
objective: A common table expression names intermediate relational results and makes a multi-step query easier to review. A CTE does not automatically enforce security or improve performance.
misconception: The starter aggregates all tenants before filtering and leaks beta's project through the report.
acceptance: Explain CTE versus inline subquery, why a CTE name is not a persisted table, and why placement of tenant filters matters. Read EXPLAIN before making performance claims about materialization.
securityBoundary: A beautifully factored CTE can still return unauthorized data if its predicates are wrong.
